body:
**Impact.** The `[[leaves.plan_advisory]]` leaf (#301) produced **no artifact on 9 of 9 bundles** in the self-hosting instance (462, 466, 474, 475, 476, 494, 495, 497, 506) since it went live 2026-08-13 — every one of the nine `plan-advisory-plan-reviewer.md` files is the byte-identical NOT-COMPLETED placeholder (same md5). Each run burned ~6.5 min of sonnet/high and cost a human §6 adjudication, and the placeholder tells that human the **opposite of the truth**:

> Failure class: **substantive — needs a human.** The leaf ran but did not yield a usable verdict; do not assume an infra blip.

It *is* an infra blip. `plan-advisory-benefit.json` now records "0 findings / brief revised: no" nine times running — evidence that would wrongly convict the feature at an Act review.

**Cause (reproduced, not inferred).** Three facts compose:

1. `_seed_plan_sandbox_settings` (`template/src/pdca_harness/leaves.py:2419-2454`) makes the plan-advisory leaf the **only** leaf that turns the vendor sandbox **on**, fail-closed: `{"sandbox": {"enabled": true, "allowUnsandboxedCommands": false, "failIfUnavailable": true}}` plus `--setting-sources project`. Check-side advisory leaves call `_seed_sandbox_settings`, which writes **no file at all** when the instance grants nothing (`leaves.py:2282-2285`), so they inherit the operator's ambient settings where `sandbox.enabled` defaults false.
2. On a host that denies unprivileged user namespaces — Ubuntu's default `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1`; `unshare -Ur true` → `Operation not permitted` — bubblewrap cannot start, so under that fail-closed policy **every** Bash call fails, including `echo hello`. `failIfUnavailable: true` is doing exactly what it promises; nothing reports that it fired.
3. The leaf has **no other write route**: argv `--allowedTools Read,Bash,Grep,Glob` and `agents/plan-reviewer.md.jinja` frontmatter `tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob`, while `_plan_advisory_prompt` (`leaves.py:2915`) and the agent's "## Output" section both require it to *write a file*. Bash is the single mechanism, and it is dead.

The leaf then **exits 0**, so `_run_plan_advisory_sandboxed` (`leaves.py:3152-3155`) takes the `else` branch and files "produced no artifact" at `_FAIL_SUBSTANTIVE`.

**Reproduction** (any host with `apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`):

```sh
T=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$T/.claude"; cp -r <instance>/.claude/agents "$T/.claude/agents"
echo '{"sandbox":{"enabled":true,"allowUnsandboxedCommands":false,"failIfUnavailable":true}}' > "$T/.claude/settings.json"
cd "$T" && claude -p --agent plan-reviewer --permission-mode acceptEdits \
  --allowedTools Read,Bash,Grep,Glob --model sonnet --setting-sources project \
  'write plan-advisory-plan-reviewer.md in your cwd containing "- NEEDS-HUMAN — probe"'
```

The leaf answers: *"The Bash tool is entirely non-functional in this environment (sandbox setup itself fails with a seccomp/userns permission error before any command runs — even `echo hello` fails). I have no Write/Edit tool available to create files directly. **The write did not succeed.**"* — rc 0, no file. Drop `--agent` and the same run **succeeds**: without the agent's `tools:` restriction the model has `Write`, which `acceptEdits` auto-approves — which is why this never showed up in the Check leaves or in testing.

**What would fix it** (maintainer's choice — not asserting the shape):

- **Classify it honestly.** A leaf whose sandbox never started is `_FAIL_ENV`, not `_FAIL_SUBSTANTIVE`. A cheap probe before the real run (seed the sandbox, run `true` through it) turns nine misleading §6 items into one accurate "the vendor sandbox is unavailable on this host" line.
- **Give the leaf a write route that isn't Bash.** Either add `Write` to the plan-advisory argv + agent `tools:` (the "no Write/Edit" contract in the prompt exists to stop it editing `brief.md`, which `permissions.deny` or the prompt already covers), or have the harness capture the leaf's stdout as the artifact when the file is absent.
- **Preflight it.** Nothing in `doctor` checks that a configured leaf which *requires* the vendor sandbox can actually start one on this host — see #452; happy to have that half live there.

Filed from the self-hosting instance's Act review 2026-08-15 (pdca-pdca `process/act-log.md`).
title: plan-advisory leaf is inert on a userns-restricted host: fail-closed sandbox kills its only write route, and the empty result is reported as 'substantive — not an infra blip'
